name: Fettle

adaptedFrom.name: PaperCSS
reused: The irregular border radius technique that makes a plain rectangle read as a drawn one (src/core/_mixins.scss, the border-style mixin), rewritten as the six --edge tokens at the top of style.css
Cycling those variants across sibling elements so no two neighbours share a wobble (src/utilities/_borders.scss, the child-borders rules), rewritten as the nth-child(6n + N) blocks in style.css
The flat offset shadow rather than a blurred one (src/utilities/_shadows.scss and the shadow mixin), rewritten as the --shadow and --shadow-deep tokens
The idea the whole library rests on: that a sketchbook surface can be built from borders, radii and shadows, with no images at all
notReused: The stylesheet itself. Nothing from dist/paper.css or src/ is shipped here; the cues above were re-implemented

Its remote font import. Line 1 of src/core/_config.scss pulls Neucha and Patrick Hand SC from fonts.googleapis.com, which would make every visitor of every site built from this template request a third party host. This edition bundles one OFL typeface locally instead
Its palette, its typography, its form kit, its navbar, modals, popovers, tabs, alerts, badges and progress bars
Sass, npm and its build pipeline
Every word of PaperCSS documentation copy, and every image in its repository

photography: None. This edition contains no photographs, no generated images, and no assets taken from any reference site. Every graphic is an SVG file written by a script in tools/: the drawn furniture by Rough.js, the people from Open Peeps.
remoteRequests: None. No remote scripts, fonts, trackers, maps, analytics or form services. The one typeface is bundled locally, both scripts run at build time, and every contact link is a mailto: link to an example address. The only http and https strings anywhere in this folder are inside licence and provenance files, pointing at the upstream projects credited above.

fonts.origin: @fontsource-variable/bricolage-grotesque 5.3.0, the latin subset with the weight axis, archived at upstream/fontsource-bricolage-grotesque-5.3.0.tgz
fonts.why: Bricolage Grotesque is a grotesque assembled out of parts that do not quite agree: flared terminals, uneven joins, a slightly heavy waist, and an optical size axis that was designed to be pushed. It carries a drawn page without pretending to be a handwriting face, which would be unreadable at body size and would fight the actual drawings. It has no reserved font name, so it can be modified and redistributed inside an exported site with no renaming duty. One family across the whole edition, with the weight axis carrying every level of hierarchy.

referenceDirection: A community workshop and class programme drawn rather than photographed: squared paper under everything, a workbench in elevation as the house drawing, cards with the uneven corners of a rectangle sketched by hand, rules that drift, a floor plan and a bar chart in pencil, and a class full of people who are all illustrations. No reference site code, imagery or branding copied.
demoContent: Fettle, its classes, tutors, timetable, bench numbers, address, opening hours and fees are illustrative examples, not a real organisation. Every fee on the page is marked illustrative where it appears. No visitor numbers, awards, sponsors, client names or testimonials appear anywhere, and nothing on the site can take a booking or a payment.
